clue.text: Moved by (hearing) 18 15, (one who) 10 23 (takes in) 6 17 — now?

definitions.note: the puzzle appeared for Christmas Eve, so the answer names the day it is being solved

indicators.note: something moved has been shifted about, so the letters of the cross-referenced words are rearranged

parts.note: 18 across is VASTER and 15 across is CHIMES, read together as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A churchgoer stirred by louder bells, a believer and preachers' sermons, all on one festive night.
explanation.walkthrough: Each pair of cross-references (18 15 VASTER CHIMES, 10 23 CRAVES THEISM, 6 17 VICARS THEMES) holds exactly the same twelve letters, so 'Moved by' rearranges any of them; the bracketed words just make a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was published on 24 December, so the question mark asks the solver to name that very day.

clue.text: Vehicle I'd taken round river, upset female figure

indicators.note: taken round means the vehicle and I'd enclose the other piece

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
I'd contracts to ID with the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the river's name reads backwards

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Someone toppled a statue while driving their car around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the Scottish river reads upward; 'taken round' wraps the car and I'd around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A caryatid is a carved stone column in the form of a draped woman, as on the Erechtheion in Athens.

clue.text: Woman pursuing expensive cars has to move on wheels

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the woman's name comes after the cars

parts.note: Rollers is slang for Rolls-Royce cars
Kate is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A gold-digger chasing luxury cars has to keep moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To roller-skate is to glide along on skates fitted with small wheels.

clue.text: Errors student has avoided in small quantities

indicators.note: avoided means kept out, so the student's letter is dropped from the errors

parts.note: slips are errors
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A careful pupil has avoided making mistakes in little ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Sips are tiny mouthfuls of a drink, hence small amounts taken.

clue.text: Filmier oil would ruin coloured glass

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks its order, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A greasier oil would spoil the stained glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Millefiori is decorative glassware made from slices of many-coloured glass canes, Italian for 'thousand flowers'.

clue.text: A lot of rubbish picked up in total

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the letters read upward, backwards
a lot of, not all, means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: mush is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Plenty of litter was collected altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims MUSH to MUS, which 'picked up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the total got by adding numbers together.

clue.text: Endless sin, in that degree, will engage Rector and other ministers

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a vice is a sin

indicators.note: to engage is to take in, so the degree word holds the rector's letter

parts.note: as means to that extent, as in 'as tall'

explanation.surface: Sin without end, to such a degree, will occupy the rector and his fellow clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'other ministers': a rector is himself a minister, and the answer names ministers of another kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicars are parish priests, ministers of the same kind as a rector but differently paid.

clue.text: Timely song about a lot of cake

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: a lot of, not all, means the cake loses its final letter

parts.note: a roll, as in Swiss roll, is a cake

explanation.surface: A seasonal tune concerning a big slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a Christmas song, timely in a puzzle printed on Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Reserve right in company for a philosopher

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the company letters surround the rest

parts.note: ice means cool reserve of manner

explanation.surface: Keep the right person on staff to serve as a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was a Roman statesman and orator who also wrote philosophical works.

clue.text: Staff claim changes, in disputatious style

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective describing such writing

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

indicators.note: changes means the word is altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Employees argue over altered pay demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing is aggressively argumentative, attacking an opponent's position.

clue.text: City day out? This is the worst part

indicators.note: out means removed, so the day letter leaves the city's name

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A day trip to the city is the low point.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs left at the bottom of a wine barrel, the least wanted part.

clue.text: Requires river to pass through grottoes

indicators.note: the river runs through the grottoes, so its letter sits inside them

parts.note: grottoes are caves

explanation.surface: An underground stream must flow through the caverns.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave is to long for or need something badly.

clue.text: Backtracking, English are ready to impound small, small pieces

indicators.note: backtracking means going back, so the whole run is read in reverse
to impound is to shut in, so the ready word encloses the small letter

parts.note: set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: Retreating, the English are prepared to seize tiny bits.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'small' is the single letter; the second belongs to the definition. 'Backtracking' reverses everything built after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesserae are the small tiles or cubes of stone or glass laid in a mosaic.

clue.text: Tired out with husband about daughter — split's improvident

indicators.note: about means around, so the tired word surrounds the daughter's letter

parts.note: spent means exhausted
a rift is a split; the 's is 'is', joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: An exhausted husband rows over his daughter, and the break-up is wasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift is someone who wastes money, so used as an adjective it means reckless with cash.

clue.text: Excellent account, with documentation, about movement — vinegary stuff

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the movement

parts.note: ace means excellent
ID means identity documents
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: A first-class report, with papers, on a political movement turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the excellent, account and documentation pieces flank the movement, two letters before and four after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the compound that gives vinegar its sour taste and smell.

clue.text: Washer programme, with movable energy control

indicators.note: movable means the energy letter can shift to another place in the word

parts.note: rinse is a setting on a washing machine
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A washing-machine cycle with an adjustable power setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with movable' shifts E within RINSE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps for steering a horse, so taking the reins means taking control.

clue.text: Agrees those French may imprison that man

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut in, so the French word encloses the man

parts.note: ces is French for 'these' or 'those'
him refers to that man

explanation.surface: Those Frenchmen concur that the fellow should be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime with something is to agree or fit in with it.

clue.text: Doctor keeping Gloria under treatment, making a bloomer

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the doctor's letters surround the rest

parts.note: MD stands for Doctor of Medicine

indicators.note: a patient under treatment is being worked on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The physician looking after Gloria during her care makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bloomer' is British slang for a blunder, but here it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A marigold is an orange or yellow flowering plant, so it literally blooms.

clue.text: Topics? The writer is engaged in most of the current ones

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside, so the writer goes within the trimmed word
most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: these refers to the ones here now
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Subjects? The author is busy with nearly all of today's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the current ones' means the ones present now; 'most of' drops their last letter before the writer goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes are the subjects a piece of writing or talk deals with.

clue.text: More substantial volume? More rapid, but not loud

indicators.note: but not loud means the loud letter is swapped out for the volume letter

parts.note: faster means more rapid
F stands for forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: Turn the volume up? Speed it up, but keep it quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' swaps F out of FASTER for V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaster means larger or more immense, hence of greater substance.

clue.text: No power in profundity — one instead makes conclusion

indicators.note: instead, with 'No power', says the power letter is replaced by the one

parts.note: depth means profundity
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A deep thinker loses force; another takes over and draws the conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No ... instead' swaps P in DEPTH for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the end of life, the final conclusion of it.

clue.text: Furniture item up to now reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: so far means up to now

explanation.surface: Up till now, this piece of furniture has been marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is a long upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: Junior sky pilot initially up aboard old plane

indicators.note: aboard means inside, so the letter goes into the plane

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, rickety aircraft

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A trainee aviator takes off for the first time in a battered aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is slang for a clergyman, and a curate is an assistant, junior to the vicar.

clue.text: Zero money restricting University lecturer's wealth

parts.note: O looks like zero

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the money surrounds the other letters

parts.note: pence are money
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A university teacher's riches are limited by having no cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great richness or luxury.

clue.text: Belief is held by the opposition?

indicators.note: held by means placed inside, so is goes within the opposition

parts.note: them means the other side, as in 'us and them'

explanation.surface: A conviction belongs to the other side?
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in the existence of a god or gods.

clue.text: List players supported by United

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means placed on top of, so the United letter comes below

parts.note: men are the players in a team
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Name the team, with the club behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of dishes, or of options on a screen.

clue.text: A new church in a valley — location of mountain tragedy?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the valley

parts.note: a vale is a valley

explanation.surface: A new chapel in a valley marks where disaster struck on the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'location of' points at the valley as the place the other pieces go.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding down a mountainside, often killing climbers or skiers.

clue.text: Everything unknown disregarded by supporter

indicators.note: disregarded means ignored, so that letter is left out

parts.note: an ally is a supporter
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Everything uncertain is ignored by a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: All means the whole of something, every part.

clue.text: British actor is keeping working after bit of resting

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so is surrounds the other letters
after means the working word follows the first letter
a bit of the word means only its first letter is used

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A performer is staying in work after a short break.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is an English actor, Oscar winner for Reversal of Fortune.

clue.text: Came up about promotion that's simply balanced

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the rest

parts.note: welled means rose up, as water from a spring
an ad is a promotion
just means simply

explanation.surface: Someone surfaced over an advertisement that is merely level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-adjusted describes someone emotionally stable, mentally in equilibrium.
